results.prompt: Which data structure processes elements in first-in, first-out (FIFO) order?
results.text: Which data structure processes elements in first-in, first-out (FIFO) order?
results.explanation: A queue removes elements in the order they were added: first in, first out.

results.prompt: In a binary min-heap, where is the smallest element always stored?
results.text: In a binary min-heap, where is the smallest element always stored?
results.explanation: Every parent is less than or equal to its children, so the minimum must be at the root.

results.prompt: Dynamic programming is most useful for problems that have overlapping subproblems and which other property?
results.text: Dynamic programming is most useful for problems that have overlapping subproblems and which other property?
results.explanation: Dynamic programming needs optimal substructure (optimal solutions are built from optimal sub-solutions) plus overlapping subproblems to reuse.

results.prompt: An algorithm runs two nested loops, each from 1 to n, with constant work inside. What is its time complexity?
results.text: An algorithm runs two nested loops, each from 1 to n, with constant work inside. What is its time complexity?
results.explanation: The inner body runs n times for each of the n outer iterations, giving n × n = O(n^2).

results.prompt: Which sorting algorithm has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and is stable?
results.text: Which sorting algorithm has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and is stable?
results.explanation: Merge sort always splits in half and merges in linear time, giving O(n log n) in every case, and a careful merge keeps equal elements in order.

results.prompt: In a singly linked list, which operation takes O(1) time if you only have a pointer to the head?
results.text: In a singly linked list, which operation takes O(1) time if you only have a pointer to the head?
results.explanation: Inserting at the beginning only requires pointing the new node at the current head and updating the head pointer.

results.prompt: What is the time complexity of searching for a value in a balanced binary search tree with n nodes?
results.text: What is the time complexity of searching for a value in a balanced binary search tree with n nodes?
results.explanation: A balanced BST has height about log2(n), and each step moves one level down, so search takes O(log n).

results.prompt: What is the worst-case time complexity of quick sort when the pivot is always the smallest element?
results.text: What is the worst-case time complexity of quick sort when the pivot is always the smallest element?
results.explanation: With the smallest element as the pivot, each partition removes only one element, giving n + (n-1) + ... + 1 = O(n^2) comparisons.

results.prompt: Two different keys produce the same hash index. What is this called?
results.text: Two different keys produce the same hash index. What is this called?
results.explanation: A collision happens when distinct keys map to the same index. Chaining and open addressing are ways to resolve it.

results.prompt: Which data structure does a programming language runtime use to keep track of active function calls?
results.text: Which data structure does a programming language runtime use to keep track of active function calls?
results.explanation: Function calls follow last-in, first-out order, which is exactly how the call stack works.

results.prompt: What is the average-case time to look up a key in a hash table with a good hash function and a low load factor?
results.text: What is the average-case time to look up a key in a hash table with a good hash function and a low load factor?
results.explanation: With uniform hashing and a bounded load factor, each bucket holds a constant number of keys on average, so lookup is O(1).

results.prompt: Breadth-first search on an unweighted graph is typically implemented with which data structure?
results.text: Breadth-first search on an unweighted graph is typically implemented with which data structure?
results.explanation: A queue makes BFS process vertices in order of discovery, level by level.

results.prompt: Which algorithm finds the shortest path from one source in a graph with non-negative edge weights?
results.text: Which algorithm finds the shortest path from one source in a graph with non-negative edge weights?
results.explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm greedily settles the closest unvisited vertex, which is correct when edge weights are non-negative.

results.prompt: What is the time complexity of accessing the element at index i in an array?
results.text: What is the time complexity of accessing the element at index i in an array?
results.explanation: The address is base + i × element size, computed directly, so access is O(1).

results.prompt: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits the keys in ascending order?
results.text: Which traversal of a binary search tree visits the keys in ascending order?
results.explanation: In-order traversal visits left subtree, node, right subtree, which outputs BST keys in sorted order.
